questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
questions.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 15 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}10 \\ 15 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}6 & -5 \\ -5 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}15 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}15 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}10 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace
questions.problem:
Find the vector in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ 
that is closest to the vector $x,$ where 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly independent. 

The closest vector to $x$ in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace, which is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{30}[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace
questions.problem:
Verify whether the vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ are linearly independent, and find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -9\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we verify whether ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ are linearly independent. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & -9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 7 & -7\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+7{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, the pivot columns correspond to the linearly independent vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ that form the basis of our span.

Now, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the linearly independent columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 1 & 11\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{54}[\begin{aligned}11 & -1 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the vector in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ 
that is closest to the vector $x,$ where 

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly independent. 

The closest vector to $x$ in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace, which is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}34 & -8 \\ -8 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}18 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{38}[\begin{aligned}3 & 8 \\ 8 & 34\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}18 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
